extracted.intended_audience: poets, coaches, teams and organizers competing in the Hullabaloo (Vancouver Poetry House) poetry slam
extracted.subtask_description: Official rules and judging/behavioral guidelines for competing in the Hullabaloo poetry slam, covering performance requirements (solo/group), content and prop restrictions, timing, scoring, penalties, and conduct expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Golden Rule of Poetry Slam
rubrics_metrics.description: The points are NOT the point. The point is the POETRY!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical orientation: prioritize creative expression and the quality of the poem over competitive scorekeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / Authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Each poem must be an original creation. Referencing (or sampling) and/or parodying other poems may be permitted, so long as the poem remains clearly distinct from the sampled or parodied material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poets must ensure poems are their own work; if sampling/parodying, maintain clear distinctiveness from source material to avoid violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No props or costumes (basic prohibition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets must perform without the use of props or costumes. An object that is present in the performance area and available to all performers, such as a microphone stand, will not be considered a prop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See detailed props/costume clarifications further down for borderline cases and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No pre-recorded audio or live instrumentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets must perform without pre-recorded audio or live instrumentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creating rhythm or music with your body (beat-boxing, singing, etc.) is allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit and overtime penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Each poem must be completed within a maximum time limit. For Hullabaloo, this is three (3) minutes (plus a 10-second grace period) to read one poem. A poem that goes over time will have points deducted from the total score given by the judges. The poem/performance will lose 0.5 (point-5) points for each 10 seconds they go over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time penalties are determined by the official timekeeper, emcee or event organizer and cannot be challenged. Keep performances within the 3:10 limit to avoid automatic deductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorization not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Memorization is not required or necessary. The poet may choose to bring a sheet of paper or chapbook to the stage to read off of their phone(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reading from paper/phone is permitted; be mindful of prop/costume rules if the way you hold/use the device draws attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content restrictions (hate speech & harassment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The poem may NOT include sexist, racist, homophobic, or transphobic comments. Basically, use your common sense and don’t be a jerk, and leave your hate at the gate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expression of anger, upset and frustration is allowed, but poets should avoid explicit discriminatory or harassing language. Comply with local/provincial/federal laws pertaining to civil rights and harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring method (judge selection and tallying)
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet receives scores out of 10 from five randomly-selected judges. The high and low scores are dropped and the middle three are added together, giving the poet a total score out of 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If five suitable judges cannot be found, three judges will be selected and all three scores will be counted.

rubrics_metrics.name: No repeats within the same Hullabaloo
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a poem has been performed during a bout at Hullabaloo, it cannot be repeated during a subsequent bout at that Hullabaloo. This applies to all solo or group poems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition does not apply to performances in cyphers, open mics or other non-competitive Hullabaloo settings. Poems performed in previous iterations (past years) of Hullabaloo may be used again in later iterations, though bringing new poems is encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo poem requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Every individual member of a team must perform a minimum of one solo poem during the solo poem rounds of the preliminary slams. No individual may perform more than one solo poem during any one slam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accommodations: A poet who is physically unable to read their poem onstage due to impairment may have a substitute reader perform so long as A) the primary author is present and clearly visible to the audience and B) the reader delivers the poem without significant affectation that draws attention away from the author. A teammate or coach may accompany a poet who needs physical support, provided they remain physically neutral and do not engage as performers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group poem (team piece) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Every team must perform a group poem during the fourth round (team piece round) of each Hullabaloo slam. A group poem is any poem with two or more readers. A reader is any performer who delivers a significant portion of the poem’s words; performers who make exclusively musical or physical contributions are NOT considered readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each group poem must feature the primary author of the poem as a reader. For collaboratively written poems, anyone considered a primary author must be a reader in the performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slam Code of Honour (behavior and sportsmanship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants are asked to abide by a Slam Code of Honour committing to: revel in freedom of speech and pursuit of creative excellence; encourage and support good sportsmanship; refuse violence, interference or direct threats; allow all participants to pursue their craft without censure; comply with laws on civil rights and harassment; and abide by competition rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations include fairness, generosity in victory, and grace in defeat; the Code of Honour is intended to guide conduct and reinforce the spirit of the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Props/costumes clarifications, examples and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Props/costumes can be a grey area. Examples that could be interpreted as violations: reading from a phone held in plain view when the poem is about phone use; wearing a t-shirt with a slogan central to the poem; removing an outer layer of clothing to underscore a transformation; dramatically discarding sheets of paper as part of the performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations: place phones on a music stand or read from paper/notebook; wear different clothing or layer over slogan shirts; avoid using clothing removal as a performative device; avoid dramatized discarding of papers. Simple rule: if you have to ask whether something might be a violation, it probably is or is uncomfortably close. Key exceptions: items related to religious faith, communal identity, or medical needs are permitted, but poets should avoid clearly incorporating those items into choreographed performative acts (example: a poet with braces should avoid pointing at or dramatically displaying them).

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties, enforcement, reporting and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties for violations are determined by the severity of the infraction and may take the form of partial or total points deduction (typically a minimum deduction of 2 points), up to disqualification of the poet/team. An official 'bout team' (no less than the emcee and the event organizer, possibly including other community members) will rule on violations. Penalties may be retroactively enforced following a slam and will not be announced on stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting: a participating poet (or coach/team representative) may discreetly bring a suspected violation to the emcee/event organizer offstage no later than 15 minutes after the slam ends; do NOT publicly call out violations during the show. The identity of the person who called the violation will not be revealed if a violation is confirmed. Appeals: a penalized team may request a review by the emcee/event organizer, but the results of any review are final. Time penalties are an exception: they cannot be challenged and are based solely on the time recorded by an official timekeeper, emcee or event organizer.
